resources.string: Covers the screen when a banned word appears, so you can think twice.
Reads the text on your screen, only on this phone, and covers the screen when it finds a word from your banned list. FilterOut has no internet access: nothing it reads ever leaves your phone.

FilterOut works as an Accessibility service. Open Accessibility settings, tap FilterOut (sometimes under \"Downloaded apps\" or \"Installed apps\") and switch it on. If the switch is greyed out, see the help in the README.
Also checks pictures and video frames for banned words, using text recognition on the phone. Uses a bit more battery.

A word blocks only when it appears as a whole word. Add * to widen it: porn* also catches pornography, *porn* catches it anywhere. Accents and look-alikes such as p0rn or $ex are caught automatically. Phrases work too.
Your list is empty. Add the words you want blocked, or tap the starter list.
FilterOut has no internet permission, so Android itself stops it from sending anything anywhere. Your list stays on this phone.
This screen contained a word from your banned list.
